# Stackra

The TypeScript framework and toolchain behind Figentra (services, packages, gen, CLI, docs).

## What it is

Stackra is a TypeScript framework, shipped as the `@stackra/*` packages, plus the reference apps and services that
prove them. This repository is its monorepo, on pnpm and Turborepo.

- **A framework tier, not a product** ([ADR 0023](apps/docs/src/docs/adr/0023-stackra-is-a-framework.mdx)). Stackra
  ships packages only. The apps and services here are small reference members and test beds; they never carry a
  product feature ([ADR 0075](apps/docs/src/docs/adr/0075-stackra-ships-packages-figentra-os-ships-services.mdx)).
  Figentra OS, Figentra's private product, builds its services on the published packages.
- **Decorators-only authoring** ([ADR 0094](apps/docs/src/docs/adr/0094-decorators-only-authoring.mdx)). Modules,
  actions, endpoints and fields are decorators on plain TypeScript classes, with explicit DI tokens
  (`@stackra/container`, no `@nestjs/*` and no `reflect-metadata`;
  [ADR 0005](apps/docs/src/docs/adr/0005-di-container-and-legacy-decorators.mdx)). Input and output are Zod schemas
  ([ADR 0095](apps/docs/src/docs/adr/0095-zod-inside-field-decorators.mdx)).
- **Actions are the unit** ([ADR 0098](apps/docs/src/docs/adr/0098-actions-are-the-unit.mdx)). Behaviour is a
  decorated action with a key, typed input and output and a permission; the action pipeline supplies the typed
  caller, authorisation and idempotency, and `@AsEndpoint` makes it an HTTP endpoint.
- **Encore is generated, never hand-written**
  ([ADR 0091](apps/docs/src/docs/adr/0091-generated-encore-app-in-stackra-folder.mdx),
  [ADR 0124](apps/docs/src/docs/adr/0124-encore-is-the-generated-runtime-target.mdx)). `stackra gen` emits the
  Encore.ts application into the gitignored `.stackra/encore/`; no package or service imports `encore.dev`.
- **AI-native** ([ADR 0021](apps/docs/src/docs/adr/0021-ai-engine-and-agent-write-safety.mdx),
  [ADR 0100](apps/docs/src/docs/adr/0100-ai-model-and-ownership.mdx)). Every AI tool call is an action, under the
  same authorisation as a human caller, and a write tool needs a named human approver. The repository is built with
  AI agents too, under the rules in [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md).

Packages publish only to the Stackra registry (`https://npm.stackra.figentra.com/`,
[ADR 0453](apps/docs/src/docs/adr/0453-the-stackra-registry-one-npm-compatible-store-on-cloudflare-and-our-own-licence-engine.mdx)),
never npmjs. The plan is the [roadmap](apps/docs/src/docs/roadmap.mdx).

## Architecture

| Path                         | Holds                                                                                   |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `apps/`                      | `@figentra/console`, `@figentra/mobile`, `@figentra/playground` and `@figentra/docs`    |
| `packages/<category>/<name>` | the `@stackra/<name>` libraries; `packages/tooling/` holds the config presets           |
| `services/`                  | `@figentra/service-<name>` reference services, plain TypeScript                         |
| `workers/`                   | `@figentra/worker-<name>` Cloudflare Workers (`static`, static.stackra.figentra.com)    |
| `tools/`                     | the repository scripts and the templates `pnpm new` renders                             |
| `.agents/`                   | every AI artifact (rules, agents, hooks, skills) and the Figentra Flow specs (`specs/`) |
| `.flow/`                     | the Figentra Flow install: the constitution, `lock.json` and this README's data         |

Every member declares one tier tag, and dependencies flow one way
([ADR 0003](apps/docs/src/docs/adr/0003-tier-dependency-direction.mdx)):

```text
tier:config → tier:lib → tier:app
                       → tier:service      (apps and services never import each other)
```

The full repository map, the key rules, every root command and how a change moves from issue to merge are in the
[repository guide](docs/repository-guide.md); every rule and what enforces it is in [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md). The
code is MIT, but the Stackra logos, marks and brand images are not and the fonts keep their SIL Open Font License:
see [`NOTICE`](NOTICE), [`TRADEMARKS.md`](TRADEMARKS.md) and
[ADR 0024](apps/docs/src/docs/adr/0024-mit-license-with-exclusions.mdx).

## This repository

pnpm 12 + Turborepo monorepo. Every rule lives in this repository (`.agents/rules/`, indexed below); there are no
global rules. Full guides: `apps/docs` (`pnpm docs`). Every member keeps its code in `src/`.

Where things live (path: what it holds, tier tag):

- `apps/console`: `@figentra/console` — Vite web app; authored `src/main.ts` until v3 generates the entry (ADR 0295) (`tier:app`)
- `apps/mobile`: `@figentra/mobile` — Expo app; authored `src/main.ts` until v3 generates the entry (ADR 0295) (`tier:app`)
- `apps/docs`: `@figentra/docs` — Fumadocs (ADR 0514); pages in `src/docs/` (ADRs in `src/docs/adr`), site config `src/config/docs.config.ts` (`tier:app`)
- `packages/<category>/<name>`: `@stackra/<name>`, flat inside one category: foundation, application, communication, connectors, cross-cutting, data, developer, experience, runtime, security, state (`tier:lib`)
- `packages/tooling/*`: `@stackra/{typescript,oxlint,vitest,tsdown,commitlint}-config`, exactly five presets (ADR 0300) (`tier:config`)
- `services/<name>`: `@figentra/service-<name>` — one member per service (`example`, `health`); root module `src/<key>.module.ts` (ADR 0294) (`tier:service`)
- `workers/<name>`: `@figentra/worker-<name>` — Cloudflare Worker members (`static`: `stackra-static`, static.stackra.figentra.com), `wrangler.jsonc`, ADR 0284 (`tier:app`)
- `tools/scripts`: repo helpers (Linear, bots, spec gates, runway); the checks and `pnpm new` are `stackra` commands, templates in `tools/scaffold`
- `.agents/hooks`, `.claude/settings.json`, `opencode.jsonc`: agent hooks and config
- `.notes`: private owner-only submodule (`git submodule update --init .notes`); CI and agents never need it; never reference its contents from public docs

Rules every member follows (`pnpm validate` enforces them):

- Versions come only from `pnpm-workspace.yaml` catalogs (`catalog:<name>`) or `workspace:*`. `catalogMode: strict`.
- `turbo.jsonc` extends `//` with exactly one tier tag, then its category and runtime tags; `tsconfig.json` extends one
  `@stackra/typescript-config` preset.
- `package.json` carries `keywords`, `repository` (with `directory`), `homepage`, `bugs`, `author`, `engines` and
  `"stackra": { "kind": "package", "tier", "category", "runtimes", "summary" }`, checked against
  `STACKRA_MANIFEST_SCHEMA` and the folder (ADR 0453 decision 11, amendment of 2026-10-27; `/standards/members`).
- Every test file sits directly in a `__tests__/` folder beside its subject (`src/**/__tests__/<name>.test.ts`), anywhere in the repo; no root `tests/`, no `.spec`. App e2e lives in the app. ADR 0022, enforced by `pnpm validate`.
- A package never imports an app, a service or `encore.dev`, nor another package's `src/`.
- A JSON config is `.jsonc` (comments welcome) when its tool reads JSONC; tsconfig files keep `.json` and take comments.
  The files that must stay strict `.json`, with the reason, are `MUST_STAY_JSON` in `@stackra/repo-checks`.

The programming model v3 is the target for new code (ADR 0294, 0295, 0296): a class declares its kind by its base
class, each file sits in its kind's one home group, identities are derived and locked in `stackra.manifest.json`, and
nobody writes `main.ts` or a tool config. No member is converted yet (STA-344) and its checks are planned (STA-338,
STA-339, STA-340), so today's code and `stackra validate --repository` still show the older shapes.

Reserve an ADR number before writing the ADR: `pnpm adr:reserve <slug> --issue STA-n` lands it in
`apps/docs/adr/numbers.yaml` on main first (STA-1732); never take "the highest on disk plus one" from a branch.

Done = `pnpm verify` green on the box after the merge (format, lint, typecheck, test, build, validate, boundaries, knip; "Tests run
later" below). Conventional commits.

Scope: every package is `@stackra/*` (free) or `@stackra-pro/*` (Pro, ADR 0461), never renamed and never another npm scope; publishing goes only to the Stackra registry (`https://npm.stackra.figentra.com/`, ADR 0453) from `.github/workflows/release.yml`, never npmjs or Keygen.

Deploys (owner decision 2026-10-28, ADR 0468): agents develop and deploy end to end. Dev and staging deploys and
prereleases run without the owner; production (a deploy, promote, rollback or package release) runs in CI and waits on
the owner's one GitHub Environment approval, which an agent may start. Secret values stay with the owner, main changes
only through a merged pull request, and a workstation `encore deploy` stays denied. Until the owner applies the guard
and settings edits listed on STA-1395, the guard still asks before staging deploys.

## Tests run later: merge now, label `needs-testing`

Owner decision 2026-11-03 (STA-2083, replaces "Tests run on the box"): nothing waits on tests before it lands. No box
run before the merge and no waiting on CI: open the pull request and merge it right away
(`figentra pr merge --admin [-R figentra/<repo>] <n>`, as stackra-bot; see below), then add the Linear label
`needs-testing` to its STA issue and a `Needs testing: <what to run>` line to the pull request body. The tester
lane later runs those tests on the box (`testbed run "core STA-n" . "pnpm verify"`) and removes the label.
GitHub CI runs no tests; its checks still run after the merge and stay visible. Nothing installs or tests on a
workstation.

## GitHub identity: agents are stackra-bot

Owner decision 2026-11-04 (STA-2105): agents act on GitHub only as the `stackra-bot` App. Raw `gh` and a plain
`git push` run as the owner's login `figentra-usr`, so they mean the owner; an agent never runs them, in any
repository or directory.

- In this repository: `pnpm bot:gh -- …`, `pnpm bot:git -- push origin HEAD`, `pnpm pr:merge <n>`.
- Anywhere else (another repository, `~/Projects/figentra`): `figentra bot gh …`,
  `figentra bot git push origin HEAD` and `figentra pr merge --admin [-R figentra/<repo>] <n>` from
  `@figentra/cli`. Each mints the installation token in-process from the sops `agents` scope (`secrets-exec.mjs`); none
  prints it or puts it on argv.
- A merge-now (`--admin`) merge lands only where the repository's rulesets name stackra-bot as a bypass actor. Where
  GitHub refuses it, hand the pull request to the leader for the owner; never retry as the owner.
- The bot has no `administration`, `environments`, `secrets` or `variables` permission. Rulesets, environments,
  branch protection, secrets, variables, App permissions and production approvals stay the owner's; a production
  dispatch by the bot stops at the owner check (`github.triggering_actor`).

## How work flows

Every change goes through Figentra Flow (`fflow`, the preset preset). Specs live in `.agents/specs/`.

- Every branch and pull request carries a linear key (`STA-<n>`); branches are
  `figentra/<key>-<slug>`.
- Spec the change with `/flow-specify`, `/flow-clarify` and `/flow-plan` (it writes the tasks too), then build it
  with `/flow-implement`.
- Work in a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/<name>/`, made with `fflow start <key>`; never next to the repository.
- Merge the pull request right away with `pnpm pr:merge <n>` under the owner's merge-now rule above (STA-2083): never wait on the gate. Then add the `needs-testing` label to its STA issue and a `Needs testing:` line to its body, and remove the worktree yourself.

## Rules

- Commits are Conventional Commits with a `Refs: <key>` line. Never `--no-verify`, never `LEFTHOOK=0`.
- Secrets are named, never written: no value in a file, a commit, a log or a message.
- The git hooks run the mise-pinned oxfmt and oxlint (`mise exec npm:oxfmt -- oxfmt <files>`), so a commit needs no
  install; where mise is missing they are skipped and CI checks.
- This file, `CLAUDE.md`, `lefthook.yml`, `.mcp.yaml` and the agent setup are rendered by `fflow sync`. Do not edit
  them: change `.flow/overrides/` or `flow.config.json`, run `fflow sync`, and `fflow check` shows any drift.

## Rules index

Each rule is one file. Read the ones that fit the task before editing; not every client loads them on its own.

- `.agents/rules/ai-tools.md`: Every AI tool, server or client, is generated from its own module's declarations; nobody writes or registers a tool by hand (always)
- `.agents/rules/concurrent-sessions.md`: Managing multiple concurrent AI agent sessions (always)
- `.agents/rules/http-conventions.md`: HTTP API conventions for Stackra services (authored as action and query classes; endpoints derived by convention; Encore is generated) (always)
- `.agents/rules/linear.md`: Work is not done until its Linear issue is in the right state; agents use `pnpm linear` (always)
- `.agents/rules/module-boundary.md`: Module boundary and import rules for Stackra (always)
- `.agents/rules/naming-and-casing.md`: One naming convention for Stackra. Files kebab-case with a kind suffix, class names from the file, identities derived, machine codes snake_case, namespace lookups with ::, env and secrets SCREAMING_SNAKE. (always)
- `.agents/rules/not-built-yet.md`: Technologies rejected or deferred. Do not introduce them helpfully; route to the owner. (always)
- `.agents/rules/secrets.md`: Secret management and environment configuration (always)
- `.agents/rules/service-checklist.md`: The eight things a complete service has before it is done. (for `services/**`)
- `.agents/rules/task-vocabulary.md`: The fixed set of package.json script names every member uses, and the root commands that fan them out. (for `**/package.json`, `turbo.jsonc`)
- `.agents/rules/tenancy.md`: Two-layer tenant isolation rules, plus the scope-tree rules (free code; depth by plan). Read when adding the first tenant-owned table or touching tenant-scoped code; not loaded by default.
- `.agents/rules/third-party-sources.md`: What an agent may read, port or copy from another project, and what must travel with ported code. (for `apps/**`, `packages/**`, `services/**`, `workers/**`, `tools/**`)
- `.agents/rules/versions.md`: Version pinning and catalog rules for Stackra monorepo (always)
- `.agents/rules/workspace-layout.md`: Repository directory structure and placement rules (always)
- `.agents/rules/worktrees.md`: One worktree per active task under .claude/worktrees/, removed when the work ends, never at the cost of work or outputs (always)

## Find the task's context

- Start with `fflow context --path <repository-relative-path> --json` (or repository search when Flow is unavailable).
  Read README and applicable ancestor/member AGENTS instructions, including overrides, before editing. Read the
  rules the index above names for the paths you touch.
- Locate the owning package/service, its current contract and decisions, implementation, example and tests. Follow
  exports, callers, fixtures and generator sources for shared changes. An index is navigation, not verification.
- For collection work use `fflow context --all --query <phrase>`; each checkout keeps its own revision and authority.
  A standalone clone must use its pinned framework/preset guidance, not require a sibling checkout or private notes.
- Read a skill's `SKILL.md` only when its trigger fits; check prerequisites and version compatibility before following it.
- Keep README at meaningful package, service or component-family boundaries. Explain purpose, public entry points,
  a working example and allowed verification. Keep component contracts in types and examples; do not add one README
  or AGENTS file per component, function or ordinary folder. Preserve existing mandatory member guidance.
- Keep cross-cutting capabilities in the existing catalogue/guide: owner of each step, contracts, consumers, relevant
  authorization/failure boundaries and tests. Keep decisions in ADRs, procedures in skills and operational steps in runbooks.
- Distinguish accepted decisions, checkout implementation, passing checks at a revision, releases and deployments.
  Report missing evidence and conflicting sources. Verify only in the environment the repository permits.
